positive_controls.argument: Lifecycle controls and their known coverage limits identify consequential knowledge that must survive handoff rather than remain a final inspection result.
Controls exercised during design, implementation and operation supply configuration-specific findings that baseline accounting must preserve.
Observed control behavior and explicit coverage provide a functional input for comparing the operated system with its assured assumptions.
Threat, hazard and quality analysis identifies consequential control dependencies and missing evidence in the proposed change.
Lifecycle risk analysis identifies trust, failure-propagation or robustness conditions that belong in the shared contract.
Early threat and hazard concerns expose which requirements need discriminating evidence and where a final-only test would arrive too late.
The lifecycle risk model identifies the interaction and consequence that relevant system-level evaluation must challenge.
Threat, hazard and quality claims identify the consequential relations among obligations, controls and evidence that deserve maintained traceability.
The actual design, verification and operational controls supply substantive evidence and known weaknesses for the argument.
Lifecycle verification and operational checks detect material anomalies and supply evidence for whether a correction addresses the relevant risk.
Lifecycle risk concerns identify what the model must represent and where model validation or independent challenge is required.
The risk and control model identifies which checks, exceptions and independent judgments the pipeline outputs must support.
